experiment.title: Monte Carlo mismatch sigma and yield against the untrimmed +/-2% output-accuracy window, with a PNP / resistor / amp-mirror contributor breakdown
experiment.claim: README.md 'Target specification (ratified -- see DR-005, issue #1)' row 'Output reference' (1.20 V +/-2% untrimmed, 3sigma mismatch MC N>=300 + process corners, -40...125 degC) -- but read as a MISMATCH claim, not the corner-matrix claim issue #11 already substantiates. Process-corner sims move every device the same direction together; the untrimmed spread that actually determines whether a real part lands inside +/-2% is set by how far a real PNP, resistor, or MOS device drifts from its neighbor, i.e. LOCAL MISMATCH, which only Monte Carlo over sky130's mismatch models can quantify. Wraps issue #11's own output-voltage bench (sim/output-voltage-tc/testbench/tb_vref_tc.sch, unmodified) rather than re-deriving the v(vref) extraction. Feeds issue #13 (does the design need a trim network, and what range) and issue #15 (layout matching priority, from the contributor breakdown).
experiment.statistical_convention: N = 20 Monte Carlo samples per point, local mismatch only (section tt_mm: MC_MM_SWITCH=1, MC_PR_SWITCH=0); 1 sigma sample standard deviation (N-1), fixed setseed 20260803

mismatch_model.switch: MC_MM_SWITCH (set by the .lib section: 0 in tt/ss/ff/sf/fs, 1 in *_mm)

isolation.mechanism: per-family .param override of the PDK's own sw_mm_* coefficients, placed after the .lib include (last-definition-wins in ngspice)
